item.title: Seeking Greenlight: "The Pocket DJ"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Weird Tales

Page Layout: N/A

Elevator Pitch: A Discman plays exactly what needs to be heard; sometimes more than one bargains for.

Central Narrative:
This article describes a portable cd-player identical to a Sony “Discman” of late 1980s manufacture, with the following qualities:

+ show block
– hide block
  1. The brand name “Turing” rather than "Sony." Rechargeable batteries found with the item are identical to Energizer “AA” batteries but are branded "Integrity."
  2. The item can be powered only with an included power adapter or with two (2) of four “Integrity” batteries.
  3. The item appears to contain a cd; cannot be opened.
  4. When activated, listener hears new, and original material created by their favorite musical performer OR a favorite comedian. (This seems to depend upon the “need” of the listener: do they need a laugh, or do they need to listen to mood appropriate music?)
  5. Material theoretically produced by any individual who has recorded speech or performance from the time of Thomas Edison’s first intentional recording (“Mary Had a Little Lamb”) through the present. The living or dead status of an artist does not matter, but material is broadly contemporary. Robin Williams might have an entire routine about the current US political situation, but Benny Goodman isn’t going to perform a big band song about the Gulf War.
  6. Material cannot be replicated or recorded. Efforts to sketch out compositions invariably fail. Jokes just fall apart. However, should subject actively express a desire to listen to a “recording” again. The recording may even be accessed by multiple people aware of its existence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This can of course be incredibly restorative, but the downside is that individuals who are exposed to use for a long period of time seem to become rather jealous of the material. Like children squabbling over a new video game or toy, adults will break into heated, sometimes violent, arguments when they wish to access the material and cannot do so. This effect is quickly apparent when more than one individual listens at a time.
Additional Notes: Foundation would allow any Level 2+ staff to use the item within a controlled recreation area, with the following rules.

  1. Access limited to 1 use per week, up to 1 hour per listen, 1 staff per use.
  2. Access provided via random lottery. No weight given to rank or experience.

item.title: SCP idea- Borrasca
item.description: a abandoned coal mine in the middle of the sibirian tundra
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article,

Genre: History and action maybe horror not sure yet

Elevator Pitch: Borrasca is a mine somewhere in the Siberian tundra that was abandoned years ago because the coal viens went dry. A small community had sprung up near it, and the mine was largely forgotten about, until years later when the rock crusher began to work again, and coal began being delivered to the surface. The community tried exploring the mine, but no one came back (or someone came back but all messed up, physically/mentally). The community accepted the coal, and began to sell it. The first batch of coal came with a strange note: do not use within the town of [Redacted].

Central Narrative: it will generally be about what happens if you use the coal in the town and what happens down in the mine

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the elevator pitch is the attention grabber

Additional Notes: sry I have been gone for over a year well though this is my first submission with a little bit of help from friends (I might make a actual hook later once I have actually started writing it)

item.title: The Mirror [GREENLIGHT]
item.description: Seeking critique and a green light.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): N/A

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: There is more to a mirror than just a reflection; and there is more to a reflection than the mirror.

Central Narrative: The item is a early-Renaissance propped mirror that is able to replicate any living organism in to near perfect resemblance except for the eyes which are completely void of color or pigmentation and that the blood is made of a dark corrosive material, that is occasionally excreted from the mirror itself. It could also create any living organism from a photograph or from a live camera, however, it cannot from a artists rendition.

+ show block
– hide block

While the mirror lies dormant the copy of the being says that it is the ‘perfect version’ that the mirror sees and that the ‘inferior version’ is an imposter. It also states the current feelings of the mirror with a possibility, especially when angered or hurt, to create a small humanoid made of the corrosive material to tell them the mirrors feelings and exhibit the same emotional states as normal humans.

In extreme emotional distress the black corrosive material would be secreted and any being made from the Mirror would disintegrate, along with the copied being. When a copy was asked why the Mirror did it ,the copy said it was the ‘great equality’ saying that both the ‘inferior’ and ‘perfect’ can’t exist together to preserve the Mirrors art. However, if the being was killed the remaining being will survive for 2 days before succumbing to the ‘great equality.’

However, when asked if the beings were killed no answer was given so a theory that a pocket dimension existed was created.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The whole SCP is more of a mystery and while it might not be deadly it could cause significant harm to others where, due to it’s long lifetime, most likely helped shape the world in the disappearances of historical figures to having many animals and living beings replicated. It also doesn’t go down the traditional path of constant murderous SCP’s and dwells in the more elaborate and sentient sides of the Foundation.

Additional Notes: I will most likely expand it to make a final judgment on the ‘great equality’ and make some tests and addendums. I would like to thank the reviewer(s) who looked over this and critique it. This project of mine has grown since my first attempt and any changes I can make will only help. Thank you.

item.title: Arctic Horror SCP
item.description: Seeking Article Greenlight or Critique
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Survival

Elevator Pitch: To what lengths will we go for survival? For duty? Intimate horror in this SCP will show that the natural world can be far more dangerous than the anomalous.

Central Narrative: Containment procedures explain that personnel are to be deterred from ingesting at all costs. The anomaly is a group of cryogenically frozen herbs with healing properties when ingested. Its Yukon containment facility is wrecked in a storm but one instance is recovered by a researcher and a containment engineer. The recovery log details the two struggling to escape the secluded region and the researcher’s slow demise to the elements along the way. The engineer cremates the researcher as per his dying wish, but the researcher had consumed the herb prior to death and revived himself, a breach of containment. The engineer must dissect the researcher and return what remains of the herb, as per containment procedures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Horror would be derived from the natural harshness of the setting and the desperation of humans rather than the anomaly itself. Ultimately this grounded, personal horror should better chill the reader than a simple “scary anomaly.”

item.title: "Monster House" (placeholder nickname) Looking For Greenlight
item.description: A house that appears and disappears
item.content:encoded:
A house that appears and disappears, and creatures come out to abduct people

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The main SCP a dingy old house that periodically teleports from one place to another, usually in the middle of woods, or abandoned areas. You can't see in the windows, and opening the door reveals a black void leading to another dimension. Within the void is a race of bipedal, dragon like creatures (SCP-XXX-1) that can shapeshift. They typically take the form of human children and wander the woods asking people to help them find their parents. They then take the victim to the house and abduct them into the void, no one who has entered has ever come out.

Central Narrative: will include mission logs detailing the first encounter with the SCP, and an attempted recovery of one of the creatures. After capturing the creature, it is discovered that they disappear if they go further than 1km away from the house. This information, along with another piece of info, leads to some theorizing that the house may have been built to trap the entities inside, rather than the entities using it as a pathway to our dimension.

Hook: The hook is mainly how creepy the idea is, having a child come up to you in a forest and asking you to help them find their parents, only to turn into a dragon creature and take you into an endless black void.

Additional Notes: I have a mostly completed article on my sandbox, just needs the encounter log, some proofreading, and some streamlining.

item.title: Greenlight Request: A Second Reflection
item.description: Made an SCP, need greenlights for it. A creature that can only be seen in its reflection.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid creature with smooth black skin and no features except for its mouth. You can only see its reflection, although it does not work when the reflection is recorded. As such, an image cannot be provided unless it is an illustration of the specimen.

It can phase through everything that isn't living flesh (e.g. LIVING animals, LIVING humans), but this ability is nullified if its temperature is lowered below -50 degrees Celsius, or 223 degrees Kelvin.

It acts like an aggressive and predatory animal despite its humanoid form, and will attack anything, including other SCPs. It will claw at the walls of its cell (made of mirror-like reflective metal to ensure its presence), and if it breaks the cooling system, it can breach containment.

Central Narrative: The details of SCP-XXXX's containment are yet undisclosed, but many researchers in the Foundation have suggested that it be reclassified to Thaumiel due to its aforementioned aggression. While the subject is still up for debate, its classification remains Keter, due to its extreme aggression and repeated attempts at breaching containment.

At some point, some people suggested that SCP-XXXX could be the last piece in the puzzle that is the destruction of SCP-682, but due to the incredibly high likelihood of failure, the possibility has been dropped completely.

item.title: SCP Greenlight Request "The Toybox"
item.description: Seeking greenlight for an SCP concept. My first contribution.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Weird Tales/Horror

Page Layout: N/A

Elevator Pitch: An antique toybox is not as harmless as it appears.

Central Narrative: The item in question is an antique toybox, constructed of seasoned, naval grade wood and secured with pig iron fittings. It features an integrated locking mechanism.
The toybox contains a variable number of toys appropriate to its size. Contents vary: when locked, they may change; when used without lock mechanism, they remain the same.

+ show block
– hide block

The locking and unlocking process is somewhat disquieting. In order to be unlocked, the individual physically turning the key must be an individual twelve years of age or younger OR such an individual must be present within the room.
In order to -lock- the box, the individual turning the key must be an adult (aged eighteen years or older). Furthermore, all items that were discovered within the box must have been removed, and then returned.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Each of the toys might seem harmless enough, but was in fact in its time notoriously unsafe. Where historically appropriate, the item may have been recalled. This might include items such as: a lazertag set with ultra-realistic guns; a batman cape which, when worn, tends to convince the wearer they can glide safely from a height to ground; a bag of marbles that look very much like candy; a set of lawn darts;etc.

The Foundation's concern regarding this item is that posses a significant danger. Each of these items seems to draw attention to itself, and an individual who opens the box is always presented with a compulsion to use at least some of the items that they discover. This seems to vary by person, age, and circumstance (children are most often affected, though adults, too, have been affected, particularly with prolonged exposure.) Inevitably, use of the item will result in self-harm or the harm of others.

A series of incident reports will be attached to this SCP. They include, for example: a perfectly rational researcher strapping on the Batman cape and throwing himself from the top of the motorpool building, breaking both legs, in the mistaken apprehension that he can “glide.”

Additional Notes: Notes will indicate spectrographic analysis showing use at least as far back as the early eighteenth century.

item.title: SCP-5217
item.content:encoded:
I had this idea in July when I read SCP-1423 and saw a photo a former classmate posted on the same day (not the one in the article, for licensing reasons). It just wouldn't get out of my head, so I decided to flesh it out fully, then to work to make it unique, then to put it in Wikidot format in a sandbox. Figured I might as well cold-post it and see if it sinks or swims.

I don't know if this story continues or not, but if it does, I'm sure that it happens in the Academics version of War on All Fronts. But this won't even survive 24 hours so it's pretty silly to think that'll happen.

Lots of people to thank, first among them my friend Alice for drawing the sketch at the end. Next up is RJB_R for writing the SCP that inspired this, even if it has evolved quite a bit since then. Then qntm, who gets a shoutout through Site 41 in the article, for being so dang cool. Also thanks to the people who made the Wiki Syntax guide (I stole all your code no regrets!) and the people who wrote the How to Write an SCP guide for saying that sentient beings have to be Euclid and Foundation personnel aren't stupid. Breaking rules is fun if you're clever about it and don't care about the result!

Have a great day and a great life, and if you upvote, a good month as well!

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Salvation from Ceres
item.description: I made an SCP a few months ago that was deleted. I want to seek advice so I can fix it and resubmit it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror / Suspense

Page Layout (Optional): Normal, but if someone can tell me how SCP-5999 was made, I might be able to do something like that.

Elevator Pitch: If you look at a picture of Dwarf Planet Ceres, you'll see a mysterious group of lights in the Occator Crater. I created an SCP based on the lights on Ceres.

Central Narrative: Station Tau is an international research base located in the asteroid belt that is dedicated to multiple scientific pursuits, but mainly SCP-XXXX. Station Tau and Ceres were brought to the Foundation's attention after satellites reported after SCP-XXXX, a hot liquid substance was found being ejected from the Occator Crater on Ceres at a high altitude, almost like a volcano erupting. The Foundation then made a deal with officials from Station Tau that the Foundation would cooperate with all of Station Tau's initiatives, and in exchange, Station Tau would allow Foundation Personnel to investigate SCP-XXXX. SCP-XXXX will evaporate any non-planetary material, because of its high temperature. It can hijack all communications systems and broadcast visual and auditory signals that [DATA EXPUNGED] most who hear it. Those who were left unaffected recall seeing an organic lifeform burrowed at the core of Ceres or hearing a female voice speak about its disdain for life. It also creates clones of people who have been near SCP-XXXX (at a safe distance). The moment when SCP-XXXX hijacked Station Tau's communication systems is referred to as Comms Incident One. Shortly after Comms Incident One, a patrol station referred to as Occator-Alpha was placed, and personnel onboard the patrol station were tasked with collecting SCP-XXXX safely so it could be studied. However, when they attempted to extract SCP-XXXX, the station was destroyed and the comms went offline. The maximum height at which SCP-XXXX is being ejected from the surface of Ceres started rising the day Occator-Alpha was destroyed, and has been continually rising at an identical rate since. SCP-XXXX will eventually reach Earth in ██ years. As such, a contingency plan entitled Operation Theta was created in order to ensure the survival of Earth. The main element of the 'story' of SCP-XXXX is the use of the Station Tau Archive Database and Viewing System or STADaVS. It is used by various personnel to access files and either save or delete them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The danger posed by SCP-XXXX and the element of suspense as you read down the article.

Additional Notes: If you want a draft, I can give the draft.

item.title: Let's Go on an Adventure! (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Are you brave enough?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A mysterious backpack allows individuals to embark into an anomalous dungeon when they wear it. Each of its six pockets can provide the right tool or object for the immediate situation as they progress, necessary as the dungeon itself is filled with dangerous and undiscovered creatures. Though they don’t realize this gauntlet is more preparing them for what’s to come when they reach the final chamber.

+ More Info
Hide

Central Narrative: Discovered in the Mohave Desert by an excavation team, anyone who wears the backpack and walks through the next doorway disappears into an underground passage that changes structure with every embarkment. There are fifty corridors they must traverse to escape, unable to return through each room’s entrance. Each room may entail puzzles or monsters of unknown origin, and adventurers are advised to use each pocket of their pack sparingly because each one only gets one use per journey.
Once they arrive at the fiftieth and final floor, they come across an ancient underground metropolis that now stands abandoned and derelict. The individuals here were all successful explorers that made their city out of the riches of their exploits, however met a gruesome end when a reality-warping chimera they couldn’t defeat followed them to town. The town was buried in an earthquake, the monster trapped with them, and everyone perished under its distorted claws. This backpack was one of the only pieces of gear left intact after this incident.
On the day someone kills the beast, they will find an exit to the surface, and the backpack will lose all anomalous properties. However, nobody who’s taken the backpack has returned alive. The pack reappears where it was taken with no damage, after the wearer has remained dead for at least two hours.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The backpack desires to bring someone strong enough to take down the powerful beast and avenge the lives of the fallen explorers.

item.title: Ocean's Cell
item.description: Wormhole connecting a family pool to the sea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type:SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:SCP-XXXX is a wormhole of anomalous nature located on a deep-sea level, it has the appearance of a 2 km deep round trench. Any organism or structure that trespasses it fully will shrink down to a 0.001% of its original size. Set hole will unexplainably start to inhale during 2-3 hours specially during June, July and August.

This wormhole is connected to SCP-XXXX-A, (a standard plastic family pool) which is property of a Caucasian family located in ████████████████. After diving 1 km into the pit 1 km, the walls will start to resemble the tube of a filter pump. Once entering SCP-XXXX-A through the filter hole, it appears to have a size of 2000km long, 1500km wide and 1000km high from set perspective.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-A possesses a thin plastic layer partially covering the surface, aswell as many human and insect organic tissues of massive size floating at the surface or underwater, and a chlorine dispenser originally used as a safe base to monitor the surroundings.

There are 5 inhabitants in SCP-XXXX, labeled SCP-XXXX-1 through 5. These are 4 caucasian human individuals (2 male and 2 female) and a canine creature (from the Canis lupus familiaris race). These entities only appear during certain daytime hours in the summer season, and communication with these individuals at first was impossible and dangerous.

The wormhole's origin was later discovered by reaching the surface and achieving connection. The foundation sent a team towards the location and acquired the anomaly, as well as capturing the family to interview them about the item. The pool was brought into a containment cell and since then it has been studied its size-shifting properties.

Central Narrative:During the first encounter with the wormhole, the foundation sent multiple teams to enter SCP-XXXX. Once arriving to the other end, they were amazed at the ocean despite being empty and confusing. Other than that, no other anomalies were present until the appearance of SCP-XXXX-1 to 5, which were a threat to the team since the entities weren't aware of them, causing many casualties. After receiving information about the location of SCP-XXXX,it was successfully contained.

Hook-Attention-Grabber:This anomaly is simple, a wormhole that connects the ocean to a pool. However, the most interesting part is the many changes this SCP goes through the more understood it is, until completely containing it. If done correctly, it should be classified as a Euclid, then reclassified Keter, and finally Safe.

Additional Notes:This SCP has a lot of layers and changes. It may be a bit confusing due to everything it presents so i'll need to do it correctly. I'm fairly new here so I understand if there are problems with the idea, so please tell me since i want to improve on this concept.

item.title: "The Gardener" [Seeking Greenlight]
item.description: A humanoid that must create less-than-obedient "drones"
item.content:encoded:
A humanoid that must create less-than-obedient "drones" from plants and the unfortunate actions that follow.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Split across multiple iterations of the document spanning across 10 years as containment procedures and behavior of the SCP object change.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid who, by being near plant matter, accelerates their growth dramatically, and rather than bringing them into old age, makes matured plants into sentient "drones", dubbed SCP-XXXX-1, later -2 and -3, as the nature of the anomaly changes. While it begins as a child who turns plants into not terribly threatening sentient and hostile plants, later creations of SCP-XXXX display anomalous growths and sapience, making them more threatening. SCP-XXXX is not able to stop these events from happening, as it must be near living plants in order to live, and has no control of these creatures, often being prone to attack from them.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is given its anomalous properties through the containment breach of a reality bender in a site near SCP-XXXX's home. A month after this breach, the Foundation investigates reports of deaths in a forest inhabited by SCP-XXXX, who had inadvertently converted several plants into SCP-XXXX-1 instances. An MTF unit is sent to find the source of these deaths, containing SCP-XXXX. Containment procedures begin simple, with only a modified humanoid containment chamber with a grass floor, as grass is found to be a non-issue when converted to SCP-XXXX-1. While SCP-XXXX grows over the span of a decade, containment procedures become more complex as it begins to generate SCP-XXXX-2 and -3 instances, eventually resulting either in the object's termination or a command to terminate it should it attempt to breach containment.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main draw of the concept is SCP-XXXX-1+, and how their severity impacts the life and conditions of SCP-XXXX, who isn't really a catalyst for any events as much as its creations.

Additional Notes: My biggest concern is that sapient, hostile plant-monsters feels like a concept that's simply not threatening enough to warrant the drastic actions that I want the narrative to take. I've been toying around with different ideas on this matter, foremost being to make SCP-XXXX marginally stronger than a small group of people with sufficient plants nearby, and/or to slowly give SCP-XXXX plant-like qualities, causing its anomaly to take effect on itself, posing a security threat, but these are distateful to me both for fear of X-man syndrome, as well as the fact that the narrative simply isn't really that much about the humanoid. Any advice on this situation specifically would be greatly appreciated.

item.title: The Island of Lies (Seeking Greenlights)
item.description: An Island that scrambles one's memories and leaves them much different than they were before.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

+ Elevator Pitch
- Hide
  • An island that will attempt to put any visitors to sleep. They will wake up on an identical island a ways away with some of their memories changed out. This can be anything from simple things like where they put their keys to aspects of their identity and personality itself.
  • People can go through this process an infinite number of times, further altering their memories and personality each time.
+ Central Narrative
- Hide

My goal with this is to focus on two subjects the Foundation has been using to test the SCP.

The first subject is a person who has been hit incredibly hard by the memory alterations, to the point where very few of his original memories still exist. This subject is being rehabilitated by Foundation staff in an attempt to see if he can be restored to his former self or if the changes are permanent.

The other subject is being used to test the effects of repeatedly sending the same person to the island. This subject also has barely any of his original memories remaining and has changed names at least three times, but rather than attempting to "fix" him, the researchers are simply layering on more and more changes to his brain. This part of the article would probably be more comedic in tone than the rest.

+ Hook/Attention Grabber and Additional Notes
- Hide

The big things I want people to be drawn to are the mystery of why and how the memory changes are being made as well as the stories of the two test subjects.

Additional Notes:
I want to know if the second island is really necessary, considering how small of a role it plays in the big picture. I was also playing around with the idea of the SCP being sentient and afraid of rising sea levels, let me know what you think of that idea.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight ("The Boo Hag")
item.description: Looks can be deceiving, but not in the way you may think.
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I’m a long-time lurker and looking for critique on the concept for my first SCP. All feedback is welcome.

Seeking Greenlights: YES

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Traditional SCP document layout.

Elevator Pitch: What is perceived as a horrid monster in Gullah culture/Carolinian folklore is, in reality, a caring mother. While not necessarily benevolent, this SCP does whatever it takes to care for its child.

Central Narrative:

+ Open
- Close

The narrative is intended to be told throughout the entire document, from the containment procedures, to the description, to a small collection of recovered documents and interviews. The SCP itself is what can be described as a “boo hag:” a skinless, humanoid entity that has the ability to disguise itself using victims’ skins, bewitch others using its voice, and transfer the life force it drains from victims to strengthen and heal other boo hags. Through the RD’s and interviews, the reader learns that the SCP and its daughter were hunted by humans; the latter was killed while the former escaped at the cost of losing her tongue. Having lost its daughter and ability to bewitch, the hag bides its time and waits for another chance to raise a child. Sometime later, the hag infiltrates a family under the guise of the patriarch’s late wife’s sister and cares for the patriarch's daughter, who is suffering from a terminal illness. The hag uses its powers to drain and transfer the life forces of local victims into her new daughter, but fails to keep her alive. The daughter expires, and the hag is apprehended by authorities following missing persons accounts. The Foundation intervenes and contains the hag; investigation of the daughter’s body reveals her to have been a young boo hag. The reader is left to decide whether or not the man’s late wife was also Boo Hag and to question the origins of the “Daughter Hag.”

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ Open
- Close
  • Explores a twist on the “murder monster” cliche and on a lesser known creature associated with Gullah culture and Carolinian folklore
  • The SCP builds up to a final reveal that will (hopefully) explain why the SCP is passive in containment (has no desire to lose another child), give a reason for the SCP to use its powers in the first place, why it infiltrated that certain family, and offer the right amount of ambiguity so as not to water down the intrigue of the SCP down with a concrete answer.

Additional Notes: I realize that choosing to write a humanoid SCP as my first article may be looked down upon, but I believe that I have what it takes to tell a compelling story.

item.title: The Dover Demon
item.description: The creature known as "The Dover Demon" witnesses the history of the world.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy/History

Elevator Pitch: SCP-X is the creature known as The Dover Demon. SCP-X is a sapient small humanoid with bright white eyes lacking pupils, with a large skull and and no mouth, however it is able to speak, with its face moving as if it is speaking. SCP-X is also able to become invisible, to hide itself from others. SCP-X is very friendly. SCP-X has a high interest in floors, and anything on them, such as rugs, crumbs, shoes, and the shoes people are wearing.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

The main focus of the article will be centered around an interview conducted with SCP-X. SCP-X is asked about where its from. This leads to a short explanation that he was born in a cave, and that he left the cave once he was around 19. He then begins talking about how as he traveled, there was a lot of sounds, but he was focused on the grassy fields and the smell of fresh soil.

He then talks about how he came to a city where people had spectacular black shiny shoes, and that the ground was organized, he goes on about how he walked for a bit but eventually came to water, so he boarded a ship he thinks was called the "Mayflower". He journeys on the Mayflower for a bit, and eventually lands at Plymouth, where he stays for a while, albeit disappointed that the ground wasn't neat and organized like the ones before, and everyone's shoes were old and messy. When the "people in the red coats with fancy black buckled shoes and long guns" came and started shoving them and shooting them, he presumed it was because they had messy shoes.

He then goes on to describe the events of the Boston massacre, however only detailing that the people in red coats shot the people with messy shoes, and got blood all over the ground. He then explains a few more details of his life after that such as how he believed the red coat people left because people finally started getting newer shoes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the attention grabber that the foundation literally has a little guy who was aboard the mayflower and was present at the Boston Massacre, but is just talking about everyone's shoes.

Additional Notes: Just an idea I came up with, give me your critiques and tell me what you think!

Page Layout (Optional): Basic layout

Elevator Pitch:
-SCP is a sentient vintage ham radio that produces various forms of music to living things that enter its radius.
-The music in-question is based off the person's history, personality, how other people view them and in the case of other SCPs or other anomalous entities, their abilities. It can also play music to what would otherwise fit the scenario in-question (if its a containment breach its going to sound out chase music mixed in with the leitmotifs of the other SCPs that are part of the breach, etc, etc.)
-The SCP can teleport to a place that is having a suitably dramatic moment and play said music or otherwise to a person that it has played music to before and is 'bored.'

+ show block
– hide block

]
Central Narrative: As above with potentially exploring other SCP's stories and personalities through the radio's music. Eventually (I don't really know how planned interviews and addendum later down the SCP's life-line works) I'm planning for a researcher to try and ask the SCP questions, the SCP answers in a semi-convoluted way.

Standard questions apply and then… the researcher will go to ask 'do you have a song of yourself?'

The radio will reply 'no' but will than go onto say, 'but I'm sure I did have one, but I don't anymore.'

And like… that could go down so many routes, who took it? Where is it now? How do we get it? What happens when the SCP gets its 'song' back?

Does the Foundation fulfill its request? The SCP probably has some hints in its memory of where the song once was and that can go into tales or more interviews and mission ops and lot of other things.

So that's a narrative I've come up with.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I've looked over other SCPs for a while now and while there are a couple that do involve music, there are none that I could find that involve the SCP finding the theme song of basically anything in existence… except itself. Of a most important note including other SCPs that could delve into one's personality or backstory through usage of music.

Additional Notes: No particular concerns right now.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: The Watch | Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Other, General Information about SCPs with abilities.

Elevator Pitch:

  • A Watch the can open portal in space and time allowing the user to travel through time and even

different dimensions (dimensions only if the user has seen the dimension.

  • A Old Black and White Tv that houses the sales commercial for the watch in a form of a 80's style

advertisement.

  • A Male salesman in the commercial that will hand you the watch if the viewer wishes to purchase

the watch for $15.99.

  • Tv will go dormant for a few months after a purchase is made.

Central Narrative: A Watch that can create portals through space and time sold to a viewer through a black and white tv by a 1.3m tall white male with bold hair and blue eyes. After the "salesman" finishes talking about the product he will ask the viewer if they would like to purchase the watch. If the viewer agrees then the salesman will reach id hand through the tv maintaining the black and white texture and ask for a payment of $15.99. Once payed the salesman will place the money into his pocket and hand a box to the viewer then the TV will turn off and remain dormant for 2-3 months.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As far as I know there isn't really anything like this but the concept I think is pretty interesting because of how the object is obtained and what it can do. This is why i will require clearance level 4 in order to interact with the watch, tv or salesman and the SCP will receive a safe class because it's not going anywhere without help.

Additional Notes: I'm wondering if there is anything like this already on the site, if it's a good and article worthy subject and if there is anything about the SCP that would benefit from change, keep in mind i wish to keep this a safe or thaumiel class SCP. Thankyou :)
